Estrogens in men are metabolites of testosterone and other androgens. An enzyme called Aromatase circulated in the bloodstream and converts a proportion of one's natural testosterone into estrogen. Because the brain is obsessed with maintaining equilibrium, when you take steroids (or drugs which artificially jack up your body's own androgen production), the brain upregulates aromatase in order to maintain a balance, and therefore estrogen levels rise to the point at which they begin telling various parts of your body that you're a woman and that those body parts should develop female characteristics.

When you hear bodybuilders talking about "post cycle therapy", this is essentially what they are referring to - in order to prevent this from happening, it's necessary to take medications which block aromatase (Aromatase Inhibitors) as well as medications which block estrogen receptors (Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators) in order to avoid any possibility of excessive estrogen being created and being allowed to exert feminising effects on any tissue in the body. Partly because of a lack of education, and partly because such drugs are expensive and difficult to get,many lads totally neglect this aspect of steroid or prohormone use, and this is the end result.

I should point out that this is often not born out of ignorance or laziness - there are a lot of bodybuilding products out there which don't actually explicitly spell out the fact that their mechanism of action involves altering hormone levels, thus necessitating the use of anti-estrogens. A lot of supplements have either direct or indirect androgenic activity which goes undeclared to avoid falling foul of the FDA, but it means that users are taken completely by surprise when something like this happens to them. My rule of thumb is, if your supplement is anything more than protein, creatine or vitamins, you need to consider a precautionary PCT regime just in case it has androgenic effects. Any supplement which lists ingredients as either plant extracts or overly-technical sounding "sciency" names (lots of numbers and hyphens) should be treated as a potential source of androgenic activity if you can't find a source which states otherwise. For example, 17α-Methylpyrazolo[4',3':2,3]-5α-androstan-17β-ol is actually the steroid Stanzolol, so if you see an ingredient with a "jargon" sounding name, research the shit out of it and make sure you have something on hand to counter estrogen rebound just in case you're unwittingly taking something which will cause anything like this.
